chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 298: Li Huowang Sees a Harvested Heart-Element
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang shares a drunken meal with an official of the Supervisory Heavenly Office—and learns the true value of a Heart-Element: as a harvested trophy bound for the imperial treasury. Survival just got lonelier.
og_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 298: The Heart-Element’s Price
og_description: A feast turns into a lesson in horror as Li Huowang comes face-to-face with what the world really wants from him.
twitter_title: Ch 298: When You’re Worth More Dead Than Alive
twitter_description: Li Huowang sees a dead Heart-Element and realizes he’s not a person in this world—he’s inventory.

lore_anchors.definition: A rare human constitution derived from classical Daoist cosmology; the primordial substance before form takes shape. In the Dao-Twisted World, a Heart-Element’s flesh, tongue, bones, and organs are prized alchemical ingredients worth centuries of lifespan.
A euphemism for “tongue” used in jianghu code; a “Heart-Element’s fortune” refers to its tongue, considered a valuable magical material for forging talismans or tools that induce mental confusion.

A government-sponsored institution that polices supernatural activity and collects rare resources; Heart-Elements are classified as “celestial treasures” bound for the imperial treasury, making the Office both a potential ally and a direct existential threat to Li Huowang.
A metaphysical currency representing a person’s remaining lifespan; powerful magical items are often priced in decades or centuries of yang-life rather than money.
A high-ranking official within the Supervisory Heavenly Office, implied to possess a powerful tool forged from a Heart-Element’s tongue.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is the Heart-Element only a head and organs?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Tuoba Danqing explains that they tried to capture a live Heart-Element, but it was intercepted by rivals at the border. They only managed to salvage the head and internal organs from the fight.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What does “招财” (fortune) mean in this context?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It is a jianghu euphemism for “tongue.” The Heart-Element’s tongue is a prized alchemical ingredient, often used to forge tools that induce mental confusion in enemies.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Huowang feel he cannot trust the Office?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Seeing a harvested Heart-Element makes him realize that, as a Heart-Element himself, he is classified as a “celestial treasure” by the Office. Any ally could turn on him the moment profit outweighs friendship.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Does Tuoba Danqing know Li Huowang is also a Heart-Element?
cultural_notes_faq.a: No. He evaluates Li Huowang’s lack of greed as a sign of reliability, but Li Huowang’s identity remains hidden—for now.
